title: Masmark part ways with estellyy., sign HikariiFloofie
author: BPL Staff
body:
[Masmark](#/team/masmark) have made a change to their active roster, releasing AWPer [estellyy.](#/player/estellyy) and signing free-agent rifler [HikariiFloofie](#/player/hikariifloofie) in her place. The move takes effect immediately.

For much of the past year [Masmark](#/team/masmark) ran a double-AWP setup, with [estellyy.](#/player/estellyy) sharing the sniper role alongside [Xyrolizea](#/player/xyrolizea). That left the team a little light on pure rifle firepower, and this switch is aimed squarely at fixing it. [HikariiFloofie](#/player/hikariifloofie) arrives off strong recent form, posting a 64% win rate and a 1.12 K/D, and she steps straight into the rifle line next to [urnisa_](#/player/urnisa) and [kn](#/player/kn).

The change also keeps the roster tightly knit around a shared language and region. With in-game leader [XueHuaVT](#/player/xuehuavt) calling the shots and [Xyrolizea](#/player/xyrolizea) now the team's sole AWPer, [Masmark](#/team/masmark) field an all-SEA five that should communicate cleanly under pressure.

[estellyy.](#/player/estellyy) departs as a free agent after a long run with the club stretching back to 2023, a tenure that took in multiple Audax Esse Invitational campaigns. She leaves as one of Masmark's most familiar faces, and there is plenty of interest in where she lands next.

The timing is deliberate. The swap arrives midway through Bot Pro Cup 2026, giving [HikariiFloofie](#/player/hikariifloofie) a live stage to settle in and the team a chance to see whether a single-AWP, rifle-heavy look can push them up the standings.

title: Team Singapore crowned BPL Nations Cup 2026 champions
author: BPL Staff
body:
Team Singapore are the champions of the [BPL Nations Cup 2026](#/tournament/bpl-nations-cup-2026), sweeping through the bracket and dropping just a single map on their way to the title.

The run began in the Round of 16 with a clean 2-0 win over Team Vietnam. Singapore never looked troubled, setting the tone for what would become one of the most convincing title runs the Nations Cup has seen.

The Quarterfinals brought another 2-0, this time against a strong Team Taiwan. [caturteer](#/player/caturteer) and [obvMX](#/player/obvmx) led the fragging while [twentyrosie](#/player/twentyrosie) and [Aranionja](#/player/aranionja) provided the supporting firepower, and [Dirfun](#/player/dirfun) anchored the sniper role down the stretch.

In the Semifinals, Singapore met Team Indonesia, the eventual third-place finishers, and once again closed it out 2-0. The result booked their place in the final without dropping a map across the first three rounds.

The Final was the only real test. Team Korea, who had battled their way to the championship match, managed to take a map off Singapore, but it was not enough. Singapore steadied themselves and closed out a 3-1 victory to lift the trophy.

Across four rounds Singapore went 2-0, 2-0, 2-0 and 3-1, conceding just one map in the entire tournament. It is a statement result for [caturteer](#/player/caturteer), [Aranionja](#/player/aranionja), [obvMX](#/player/obvmx), [twentyrosie](#/player/twentyrosie) and [Dirfun](#/player/dirfun), and it cements Singapore right at the top of the region.

title: Astral Bloom and Lunar Cadence complete three-player swap
author: BPL Staff
body:
[Astral Bloom](#/team/astral-bloom) have overhauled their roster in a three-for-three trade with Lunar Cadence, a move aimed at reversing a dismal run that has left them at the foot of the standings.

Out go riflers [Eris Suzukami](#/player/eris-suzukami) and [Tsumugi Kokage](#/player/tsumugi-kokage), along with AWPer [Shiranami Ramune](#/player/shiranami-ramune), all three heading to Lunar Cadence. Coming the other way are riflers [Ginjo Saine](#/player/ginjo-saine) and [Kogara Toto](#/player/kogara-toto) and AWPer [Yumeno Akari](#/player/yumeno-akari).

The core duo of [Remia Aotsuki](#/player/remia-aotsuki) and [Tachibana Hinano](#/player/tachibana-hinano) stay put. Remia keeps the in-game leader role while Hinano remains the team's most reliable fragger, giving [Astral Bloom](#/team/astral-bloom) a familiar spine to build around.

The rebuild also keeps the org firmly Japanese. With [Tachibana Hinano](#/player/tachibana-hinano), [Ginjo Saine](#/player/ginjo-saine), [Kogara Toto](#/player/kogara-toto) and [Yumeno Akari](#/player/yumeno-akari) all flying the flag, four of the five starters are Japanese, alongside the Dutch [Remia Aotsuki](#/player/remia-aotsuki).

The incoming trio arrive as a package from Lunar Cadence, so the chemistry should already be there. On paper it is a clear upgrade in the win column, with [Ginjo Saine](#/player/ginjo-saine) and [Kogara Toto](#/player/kogara-toto) both winning more than half of their maps this season, a stark contrast to the sub-40% marks Astral Bloom had been posting.

Whether it lifts them off the bottom remains to be seen, but after a 7-18 record in maps, standing still was never an option.

title: Aspire look beyond Singapore, add Mikuryne and Chisa_Scarlett
author: BPL Staff
body:
[Aspire](#/team/aspire) have reshaped their roster with two signings, moving on from [Stylus](#/player/stylus) and [Moira](#/player/moira) and bringing in free agents [Chisa_Scarlett](#/player/chisa-scarlett) and [Mikuryne](#/player/mikuryne). Both departing players become free agents, and the changes take effect immediately.

The move is a response to a rough season. [Aspire](#/team/aspire) have struggled to string wins together, with the whole roster hovering around a 35% map win rate, and the team sat near the bottom of the pro standings. Something had to give, and the front office chose to target the two spots where the numbers were weakest.

[Stylus](#/player/stylus) leaves after a long run as the team's AWPer, but his form had fallen away, with a 0.74 K/D over the season that made him the roster's biggest liability in the duel. [Moira](#/player/moira), a veteran rifler with years of history in the scene, departs after posting a sub-1.0 K/D of her own. Both had been part of the core since the [Aspire](#/team/aspire) project came together, and their exits mark the end of an era for the team.

In come two riflers who bring immediate upside. [Chisa_Scarlett](#/player/chisa-scarlett) arrives as the standout Singaporean free agent on the market, carrying a 1.11 K/D and a winning record over her recent maps. [Mikuryne](#/player/mikuryne) is the bigger statement, the highest-rated free agent available anywhere in the league, and crucially she is Indonesian rather than Singaporean.

That signing is a notable shift. [Aspire](#/team/aspire) had always fielded an all-Singaporean five, and [Mikuryne](#/player/mikuryne) is the first player from outside the country to join the roster. It is a clear signal that the team is willing to look beyond its borders and prioritise raw ability over a purely national identity if it means winning more games.

The surviving core of [Hanarisu](#/player/hanarisu), [TuxedoCat](#/player/tuxedocat) and [caarrietan](#/player/caarrietan) stays in place to anchor the new-look team, with [Hanarisu](#/player/hanarisu) remaining a fixture of the lineup. On paper the new five is a meaningful step up, and [Aspire](#/team/aspire) will be hoping the fresh blood delivers a stronger, more competitive version of the team in the events ahead.

title: Nifela and the promise that built PepegaX
author: BPL Staff
body:
Every great team has an origin story, and [PepegaX](#/team/pepegax)'s begins not with a trophy but with a promise made in frustration. That promise belonged to [Nifela](#/player/nifela), an American in-game leader whose journey to the top of the Bot Pro League was anything but a straight line.

Through 2021 he was a wanderer, passing from Unorthodox to Team Elegy to Team Ragtag as he searched for a group that could hold together. The search paid off when he joined the original [Unforgettable](#/team/unforgettable) roster and, later that year, lifted Bot Pro League Minor 8. For a young leader still finding his feet it was the perfect early reward, and it looked like the start of something.

The momentum did not last. [Unforgettable](#/team/unforgettable) could not build on that Minor, and as the wins dried up [Nifela](#/player/nifela) grew convinced the roster needed changing to reach the next level. Their leader, [Sakami](#/player/sakami), did not want to make those moves, at least not then. The disagreement hardened into a real rift, and in 2022, rather than stay in a project he no longer believed in, he walked away.

He did not leave quietly. On his way out he made a vow, that he would build a team better than [Sakami](#/player/sakami)'s [Unforgettable](#/team/unforgettable). It was a bold thing to promise, and it gave him a purpose. In a twist that still colours the tale, [Sakami](#/player/sakami) would eventually make the very changes [Nifela](#/player/nifela) had argued for, yet [Unforgettable](#/team/unforgettable) have never won an S-Tier title to this day.

What followed was another spell in the wilderness. He tried his luck with Marauders of Oblivion, then Eternal Requiem, then Octagon, and none of them clicked. It was not until the BPL Legends Stage in 2023 that the pieces finally fell into place, when the group that would become [PepegaX](#/team/pepegax) came together and, for the first time since Unforgettable, the wandering leader had a home worth fighting for. Around himself he built a team with real firepower, including the rising [yuuki_ps](#/player/yuuki-ps).

Through it all, [Nifela](#/player/nifela) proved that a caller does not have to sacrifice his own output. From the leader's chair he has piled up 895 kills and 163 MVP rounds, a remarkable tally for a player whose first job is to run the team. He is living proof that the man calling the rounds can still be the one winning them.

Even then the trophy did not come easily. For two long years [PepegaX](#/team/pepegax) chased a title that kept slipping away, until at last it arrived in the most dramatic fashion possible. Their miracle run at the Audax Esse 2025 Invitational turned the promise into history. The nomad who could not find a home had built one from nothing, and he had built it into a champion. The argument, the vow, the years of searching, all of it led to that moment. The rest, as they say, is history.

title: Sketch and the Aimpunch dynasty that defined an era
author: BPL Staff
body:
[Sketch](#/player/sketch) may not be the name on everyone's lips today, but there was a time when he stood at the very centre of the Bot Pro League, and no honest account of the league's history can be written without him. As the leader of [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch), he did not just win games. He built a dynasty, and dynasties are how legacies are made.

From late August 2022 to early September 2024, [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch) were the team everyone else measured themselves against. Across that run [Sketch](#/player/sketch) carried them to multiple S-Tier titles and a Major, a haul that still leaves them among the most decorated teams the league has ever produced. When the biggest events came around, [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch) were rarely just competing. More often than not, they were the ones lifting the trophy.

The foundation of it all was a decision that took real conviction. In 2022, with the roster already competitive, [Sketch](#/player/sketch) chose to let go of [xmeijixx](#/player/xmeijixx) and [yuuki_ps](#/player/yuuki-ps) and bring in [Chiai Fujikawa](#/player/chiai-fujikawa) and [balililmao](#/player/balililmao). It was the kind of call that can define a captain, and this one defined [Sketch](#/player/sketch). Up to that point he had been the one calling the rounds himself, but he handed the in-game leader role to [Chiai Fujikawa](#/player/chiai-fujikawa) and trusted the new voice to run the team, freeing himself to focus purely on fragging. The new-look [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch) clicked almost immediately, and the pieces he assembled became the core of a championship machine.

What followed was a stretch of dominance that few teams in any era have matched. [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch) reeled off 18 straight match wins across S-Tier events, an unbeaten run that seemed like it might never end. It finally came undone against [99Lives](#/team/99lives) at Bot Pro Cup 2023, a result that sent shockwaves through the scene. But a great team is measured by how it responds, and [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch) responded in the most emphatic way possible. They fought back through the loser's stage, refused to drop another series, and stormed all the way to the title anyway. The team that beat them still watched them lift the trophy.

Through all of it, [Sketch](#/player/sketch) was the constant. With the calling now in [Chiai Fujikawa](#/player/chiai-fujikawa)'s hands, he was free to do what he had always done best, and that was frag. In his prime he was the most prolific AWPer the league had ever seen, the sniper opponents built their plans around, and his tally of MVP performances speaks to someone who consistently showed up when the rounds mattered most. Giving up the leadership did not shrink his impact. If anything, it sharpened it.

The players he moved on from went on to write their own stories too, which only underlines that his 2022 gamble was about fit and vision rather than a lack of talent. [yuuki_ps](#/player/yuuki-ps) in particular has thrived since, starring for [PepegaX](#/team/pepegax) and adding a title of her own with their Audax Esse 2025 triumph. That her path led to more silverware makes the crossroads of 2022 all the more remarkable, because both teams to emerge from that split found success.

[Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch) are quieter now, and [Sketch](#/player/sketch) no longer sits atop the leaderboards the way he once did. In recent days he has even stepped away from the sniper role that made his name, transitioning to rifling and handing the AWP to his longtime teammate [mond33__](#/player/mond33), settling into more of a support player who creates space and sets up his teammates rather than the one closing out the highlight rounds. But legacies are not measured by a single season. They are measured by the banners that stay hung long after the run ends, by the rivals who still speak your name, and by the standard you set for everyone who came after. By that measure, [Sketch](#/player/sketch) and the [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch) dynasty are permanent. He carried a team to the mountaintop and kept them there, and in the story of the Bot Pro League, that chapter belongs to him.

title: Solec, the original king of the rifle
author: BPL Staff
body:
Long before [Laburi](#/player/laburi) sat atop the rating charts, and before [rebebx](#/player/rebebx) made his own case for the crown, there was [Solec](#/player/solec). Ask anyone who was around in the early years and the answer comes back the same: he was the greatest to ever touch a rifle in the Bot Pro League. The trouble is that the numbers will never prove it, and that is the strange, quiet tragedy at the heart of his legacy.

From 2021 to early 2024, [Solec](#/player/solec) was the tip of the spear for [Divide&Conquer](#/team/divide-conquer). He was an entry fragger in the purest sense, the man who opened sites on his own, taking the first duel so his teammates could pour in behind him. It was a brutal, thankless role, and he made it look like art. Hints of that peak still flicker through the old games, a reminder of just how far ahead of his time he was.

Here is the catch. The league did not track detailed statistics during the years [Solec](#/player/solec) was at his devastating best, so there is no leaderboard to enshrine him, no rating line to point to. Those who watched know what they saw. Had the numbers been recorded, a player of his calibre would sit comfortably above a 1.25 K/D across his enormous 130-map history. The evidence lives in memory rather than in a spreadsheet, which is exactly why his story is worth telling.

In time, the fragging star followed a path much like [Sketch](#/player/sketch)'s. As he tells it himself, he began to get inconsistent, the razor edge that defined his entry play starting to dull. Rather than cling to a role that was slipping, he leaned on his extensive history in the league and moved into the in-game leader's chair, trading the first bullet for the first word.

The reinvention has been a success on its own terms. [Solec](#/player/solec) now wins rounds with his mind, his calls carving open rounds the way his rifle once did, and he has passed the torch cleanly. His successor as the tip of the spear, [LITA](#/player/lita), has been doing outstanding work on the server, the new engine to Solec's steady hand at the wheel.

For all his brilliance, the one prize has always slipped away. [Divide&Conquer](#/team/divide-conquer) are specialists in the upset, a Minor League winner and a team that has reached the biggest stages, most agonisingly the Audax Esse 2025 final, only to fall at the last step. The heartbreak of that run could have broken a lesser team. Instead it lit a fire.

They are hungry now, driven toward a title in 2026 with a passion that refuses to fade. [Solec](#/player/solec) put it best in his own words: maybe not today, maybe not tomorrow, maybe not for a long while, but one day, I will win a major. Whether or not that day comes, his place is already secure. Before the charts, before the numbers, before the names everyone now knows, there was Solec, the original king of the rifle.

title: SHOCK exit: mond33__ parts ways with Aimpunch after years of greatness
author: BPL Staff
body:
WOAH. In a move that has sent shockwaves through the entire Bot Pro League, [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch) and their legendary AWPer [mond33__](#/player/mond33) are parting ways. Read that again. One of the most decorated players in the history of the league, a cornerstone of the greatest dynasty the scene has ever seen, has suddenly been cut loose and is a free agent. Nobody saw this coming.

Make no mistake about how big this is. [mond33__](#/player/mond33) is one of only three players tied for the most event titles in league history, level with [Sketch](#/player/sketch) at the very summit. She was there for every single triumph, the sniper behind years of trophies, and [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch) touching their championship core is almost unthinkable. This is the end of an era, plain and simple.

So why break up greatness? Because [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch) do not do sentiment. Over recent play [mond33__](#/player/mond33) had quietly become the roster's least productive fragger in the duel, and a team that refuses to settle for anything less than the top made the coldest call in the book. If it can happen to a six-time champion, it can happen to anyone. That is the ruthless standard that built the dynasty in the first place.

Into the vacated AWP seat steps [Aranionja](#/player/aranionja), and she arrives with a point to prove. A Singaporean sniper with a big, proven sample and a title already to her name, she walks away from a stacked but unranked Rebellium for the chance of a lifetime. It is a pure glory move, trading a talented team still waiting for its breakthrough for the most successful team the league has ever produced. On the numbers, she is a clear upgrade in the seat.

Rebellium did not sit still either. They already run a second AWPer in [Tosaki Mimi](#/player/tosaki-mimi), and they moved fast to sign free agent [estellyy.](#/player/estellyy), recently let go by Masmark, to fill the gap. She is a proven Singaporean sniper who slots straight in beside the elite firepower of [rebebx](#/player/rebebx), and her spell on the open market proved mercifully short.

But the story of the day is [mond33__](#/player/mond33). A six-time champion, a dynasty icon, is somehow available, and the phones will not stop ringing. [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch) have reloaded and served notice that even a team with nothing left to prove will never stop hunting for an edge. Ruthless, stunning, and completely unforgettable. This is a day the league will be talking about for a long time.

title: Free agency over already: mond33__ lands at Feral Instinct
author: BPL Staff
body:
If you blinked, you missed her free agency. Barely hours after the bombshell of [mond33__](#/player/mond33) parting ways with [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch), the six-time champion already has a new home. Feral Instinct have moved fast to sign the veteran AWPer, and just like that, one of the shortest spells on the open market in recent memory is over.

It is a statement of intent from an ambitious amateur team. Feral Instinct release AWPer [Loonatic](#/player/loonatic), who becomes a free agent, and hand the sniper role to a player with more big-match pedigree than the entire amateur scene combined. This is a straight upgrade in the seat, and more than that, it is a gamble on everything a champion carries beyond raw numbers.

Because make no mistake, this is a gamble. [mond33__](#/player/mond33) arrives off the dip in form that cost her the Aimpunch seat, and nobody is pretending her fragging is what it once was. But Feral Instinct are not buying this season's stat line. They are buying six titles of composure, a decade of knowing exactly what to do when a round is on the line, and a veteran presence that a rising team simply cannot teach.

The fit is a good one. She slots in alongside the firepower of [MKakili](#/player/mkakili) and [wushii](#/player/wushii), with [qebo](#/player/qebo) calling and [TRPaki](#/player/trpaki) rounding out the lineup, and suddenly a team that was searching for an edge has a genuine leader on the roster. If her experience rubs off even a little, Feral Instinct become a very different proposition.

For [mond33__](#/player/mond33) herself, it is a fresh chapter and a fascinating one. She goes from the summit of the pro scene to leading a promotion charge from the amateur ranks, with a point to prove to a team that decided it no longer needed her. Legends do not fade quietly, and a champion with something to prove is exactly the kind of player who drags a team upward. This one is going to be worth watching.

title: miorine puts down the AWP to rifle for Cyanide
author: BPL Staff
body:
[Cyanide](#/team/cyanide) are shaking up their setup, with [miorine](#/player/miorine) set to put down the AWP and move into a full-time rifling role. After a long stint behind the big green rifle, the Singaporean is trading the sniper's patience for the pace of the entry, and it marks one of the more intriguing personal reinventions of the season.

The switch reshapes the way [Cyanide](#/team/cyanide) attack. With [miorine](#/player/miorine) stepping off the AWP, sole sniper duties now fall to [heavenweeps](#/player/heavenweeps), while [miorine](#/player/miorine) joins [Decrease](#/player/decrease) to form a beefed-up rifle line in front of in-game leader [Soozy](#/player/soozy) and the versatile [Ziweiv](#/player/ziweiv). It is a cleaner division of labour, with one dedicated AWPer and a heavier rifle presence.

For [miorine](#/player/miorine) it is a chance to reset. The AWP is the most punishing role in the game, and his numbers there had dipped over the season. A move to rifle lets him play faster, take more space, and lean on aim and timing rather than the lonely responsibility of holding an angle with the most expensive weapon on the server.

Role changes like this are never guaranteed to click, but they can unlock a player who was quietly miscast. If [miorine](#/player/miorine) settles quickly, [Cyanide](#/team/cyanide) come away with a more aggressive rifle core and a tidier structure. If not, it is a low-risk experiment for a team looking for any edge it can find.

Either way, it is a bold call to walk away from a role you have played for years. [miorine](#/player/miorine) is betting that his best rounds are still ahead of him, just with a different weapon in hand.

title: Lunar Cadence reach the playoffs as the Astral Bloom trio climb back to pro
author: BPL Staff
body:
[Lunar Cadence](#/team/lunar-cadence) have booked their place in the Bot Pro Cup 2026 playoffs and, with it, earned pro status. It is a milestone for the whole roster, but it carries a special weight for three players in particular, because this is a redemption story as much as a promotion.

Not long ago, [Eris Suzukami](#/player/eris-suzukami), [Tsumugi Kokage](#/player/tsumugi-kokage) and [Shiranami Ramune](#/player/shiranami-ramune) were shipped out of [Astral Bloom](#/team/astral-bloom) in a three-for-three trade, cast as part of the problem on a team stuck at the bottom of the standings. Rather than fade away, the trio regrouped at [Lunar Cadence](#/team/lunar-cadence), put their heads down, and ground their way back up through the Bot Pro Cup. Now they are pro again, and they did it the hard way.

Around them, [Lunar Cadence](#/team/lunar-cadence) have built a tidy unit. [Shiranami Ramune](#/player/shiranami-ramune) anchors the AWP, [Eris Suzukami](#/player/eris-suzukami) and [Tsumugi Kokage](#/player/tsumugi-kokage) lead the rifle line, and they are joined by in-game leader [briant](#/player/briant) and the young [Tatsumaki Chise](#/player/tatsumaki-chise). It is a lineup that clearly clicked when it mattered most.

And here is where it gets interesting. [Astral Bloom](#/team/astral-bloom), who kept [Remia Aotsuki](#/player/remia-aotsuki) and [Tachibana Hinano](#/player/tachibana-hinano) as their core and traded the trio away, are still languishing near the foot of the table on a 7-18 map record. The three players they moved on from just qualified for a pro playoff. It raises an uncomfortable question for the org: what if the problem was never the players who left?

It would be too easy to call it right now. The sample is small, the playoffs are still to come, and one good run does not rewrite a career. But the early evidence is hard to ignore. [Eris Suzukami](#/player/eris-suzukami), [Tsumugi Kokage](#/player/tsumugi-kokage) and [Shiranami Ramune](#/player/shiranami-ramune) have answered their doubters in the most direct way possible, and the rest of the story will write itself. That is to be seen.

title: miorine erupts for 22-6 on rifle debut against Aeternum
author: BPL Staff
body:
Well, that answers that. Barely a week after [miorine](#/player/miorine) put down the AWP to move onto the rifle, he made his debut in the new role, and it could hardly have gone better. Facing [Aeternum](#/team/aeternum) at Bot Pro Cup 2026, he exploded for a jaw-dropping 22 kills to just 6 deaths, dragging [Cyanide](#/team/cyanide) to a comfortable 13-5 win on Dust2.

A 22-6 line is a statement in any game, let alone a first outing in an unfamiliar role. That is a 3.67 K/D, topped off with 4 MVP rounds, the kind of performance that turns heads and quiets doubters in a single map. Whatever nerves might come with reinventing yourself mid-season, [miorine](#/player/miorine) clearly left them at the door.

It is exactly the sort of debut the switch was gambling on. Freed from the lonely responsibility of the AWP, [miorine](#/player/miorine) looked fast, aggressive and completely at home with a rifle in hand, taking space and winning duels all over the map. On this evidence, the move looks less like a risk and more like a player finally being handed the tools that suit him.

For [Cyanide](#/team/cyanide) the timing could not be better. With [heavenweeps](#/player/heavenweeps) settled as the team's sole sniper and [miorine](#/player/miorine) firing alongside [Decrease](#/player/decrease) in the rifle line, in front of [Soozy](#/player/soozy) and [Ziweiv](#/player/ziweiv), the new structure delivered immediately. One game is a small sample, but as first impressions go, this one was emphatic.

There will be tougher tests ahead, and one blowout does not make a season. Still, if [miorine](#/player/miorine) can bottle even a fraction of this, [Cyanide](#/team/cyanide) may have stumbled onto something special. The AWP era is over, and the rifle era has started with a bang.

title: Bot Pro Cup 2026: the group stage delivers chaos, and the playoffs await
author: BPL Staff
body:
The group stage of Bot Pro Cup 2026 is finally in the books, and what a ride it was. Eight groups, dozens of teams, and weeks of ruthless Swiss-format chaos have finally spat out the sixteen survivors who advance to the playoffs. Some of them were always going to be here. Plenty of them were not supposed to be, and that is exactly what made this group stage one of the most gripping stretches of Counter-Strike the league has served up in a long time.

Let us start with the perfect runs, because there were two of them. [Cosmos](#/team/cosmos) tore through Group B without dropping a match, a clean 5-0 that reminded everyone why they sit among the very best teams in the league. Led by the firepower of [sneakyyyyy](#/player/sneakyyyyy), they looked a class above their group and enter the bracket as the team to beat. But they were not alone in running the table. [Wraithborne](#/team/wraithborne), a North American newcomer nobody outside their own Discord was talking about a month ago, went 5-0 in Group G and did it against real competition. From unknown quantity to undefeated group winner and freshly minted pro team, their rise has been the story of the tournament.

And Wraithborne are not even close to alone in that fairytale. Seven amateur teams punched their ticket to the playoffs and, with it, earned pro status. [Prism Divide](#/team/prism-divide), [Nightshade](#/team/nightshade), [Mourningstar](#/team/mourningstar), [Syzygy](#/team/syzygy), [Lunar Cadence](#/team/lunar-cadence), [Solstice](#/team/solstice) and [Wraithborne](#/team/wraithborne) all walked in as hopefuls and walked out as professional organisations. Every one of them has a story. [Syzygy](#/team/syzygy) finally delivering on [Xyrren](#/player/xyrren)'s long-held dream of a pro team. [Prism Divide](#/team/prism-divide) topping their group behind the ice-cold [Codiant](#/player/codiant). [Lunar Cadence](#/team/lunar-cadence) carrying the reborn ex-Astral Bloom trio back to the top table. These are the runs that make a cup worth running.

The bubble was where hearts got broken. Several groups came down to the final round, and the teams that squeezed through in second on a 3-2 record all had to survive a scare or two to do it. [Mourningstar](#/team/mourningstar) edged Group C, [Artisian](#/team/artisian) held their nerve in Group E, and [Kiedz](#/team/kiedz) escaped a brutal Group H behind the elite AWPing of [Elfy Mint](#/player/elfy-mint). For every cinderella story that ends with a promotion, there is a favourite left staring at the exit wondering how a Swiss run got away from them, and this group stage had plenty of those too.

Of course, the established powers mostly did what established powers do. Alongside [Cosmos](#/team/cosmos), the S-Tier winners [The Gigarage](#/team/the-gigarage) and [Artisian](#/team/artisian) navigated through, as did a strong [Opal](#/team/opal) team and the ever-dangerous [Sacred Raven](#/team/sacred-raven) and [Moonlit Tempo](#/team/moonlit-tempo). [Flood Flashers](#/team/flood-flashers) backed up their pedigree with a second-place finish in the brutal Group A. These are teams with the experience and the ceiling to win the whole thing, and none of them will fear the bracket.

And yet for every giant that held serve, another fell flat on its face. This is where Bot Pro Cup 2026 turned genuinely brutal, because the group stage did not just produce cinderellas, it produced carnage among the household names. Six of the league's top ten teams failed to reach the playoffs, and the list reads like a hall of fame gone wrong. Pedigree, it turns out, counts for nothing if you do not show up.

The most staggering casualty of them all is [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch). The number one team in the league, the dynasty, the most decorated roster the scene has ever produced, went 1-3 in Group A and finished seventh of nine. Read that again. If you had offered anyone that result before the tournament, they would have laughed you out of the room. [New Jade](#/team/new-jade), a top-five team, somehow did worse, finishing dead last in Group C without a single meaningful win to show for it. It was the kind of collapse that ends seasons and starts hard conversations.

They had plenty of company. [Neverland](#/team/neverland) and [Lemon Tree](#/team/lemon-tree) both stumbled to 2-3 records and out, unable to string together the wins their rankings demanded. [entity](#/team/entity) went 2-2 in a nightmarish Group A and joined Aimpunch among the fallen. And spare a thought for [Infernum E-Sports](#/team/infernum-e-sports), who did just about everything right, posted a winning 3-2 record, and still missed out on a tiebreaker heartbreaker, the cruelest way to bow out of any Swiss stage. For a clutch of teams that were supposed to be circling the trophy, the group stage was a reckoning.

But if you are looking for the team nobody wants to draw, look at [division20](#/team/division20). On paper they carry the most talent of any qualifier, anchored by [Laburi](#/player/laburi), the highest-rated player in the entire league. For a season now they have been the great underachievers, a super-team that could not translate individual brilliance into results. They qualified 4-1 from Group C, and if they have finally found their rhythm at the right moment, they are a genuine wrecking ball waiting to happen. Nobody sensible is booking a match against Laburi and friends.

So here we are. Sixteen teams, single elimination, four rounds, one trophy. The bracket is a beautiful collision of grizzled contenders and wide-eyed newcomers, of teams playing for legacy and teams playing for the simple joy of having made it this far. There is going to be an upset. There is going to be a run that nobody predicts. And somewhere in these sixteen names is a champion who will look back on this cup as the moment everything changed.

Time for the part where the BPL staff put their neck on the line. On the numbers, [Cosmos](#/team/cosmos) are the clear favourites. They are the highest-ranked team in the field, they own a Major title, they were the most convincing team in the group stage, and their roster average sits near the top of the qualifiers. If you forced us to bet the house on one name, it would be theirs. Right behind them, [The Gigarage](#/team/the-gigarage) and [Artisian](#/team/artisian) have the trophies and the depth to go all the way, and either would be a worthy winner.

The dark horse, though, is [division20](#/team/division20). No qualifier has a higher roster rating, and talent like that does not stay quiet forever. Our bold shout is that this is the tournament where they finally click, and a [division20](#/team/division20) versus [Cosmos](#/team/cosmos) final would be a fitting climax between the team with the most silverware potential and the team with the most raw firepower. And keep half an eye on [Prism Divide](#/team/prism-divide), the strongest of the newcomers on paper, because cinderella does not always turn back into a pumpkin at midnight.

Prediction locked in: [Cosmos](#/team/cosmos) to lift the trophy, with [division20](#/team/division20) the dark horse most likely to ruin the script. But predictions are made to be broken, and that is exactly why we cannot wait for the first map to go live. The group stage gave us chaos, heartbreak and seven new pro teams. If the playoffs give us even half as much drama, we are all in for a treat. Bring on the bracket.

title: Opal defy the odds to win Bot Pro Cup 2026
author: BPL Staff
body:
Forget the predictions. Forget the seedings. Forget everything the group stage told us, because [Opal](#/team/opal) have just authored one of the great fairytales in Bot Pro Cup history, storming through the playoff bracket to be crowned champions of Bot Pro Cup 2026. Nobody had them here. They did it anyway.

The run was nothing short of ruthless. In the round of sixteen, [Opal](#/team/opal) drew the tournament's most feared floater, the talent-stacked [division20](#/team/division20), and dispatched them 2-0 without blinking. A 2-0 over [Solstice](#/team/solstice) followed in the quarterfinals, and suddenly the team nobody was talking about was ninety minutes from a trophy.

Then came the moment that will define this tournament. [Cosmos](#/team/cosmos) had been the story of the season, a machine riding a nine-match win streak, the longest tear anyone had been on in years and the closest thing the league had seen to threatening the all-time record of thirteen straight set by [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch)'s dynasty. Cosmos looked unstoppable. [Opal](#/team/opal) stopped them. A clinical 2-0 in the semifinal ended the streak stone dead, denied Cosmos their shot at history, and kept the dynasty's record firmly intact. If you wanted a statement, that was it.

The final was almost a formality by comparison, though the opponent was anything but ordinary. [Prism Divide](#/team/prism-divide), the breakout newcomers and the cinderella darlings of the whole event, stood between Opal and the title. It did not matter. [Opal](#/team/opal) closed it out 3-1, turning the dream final into a coronation and sending the fairytale newcomers home as runners-up.

What makes this special is who [Opal](#/team/opal) are, or rather who they used to be. Three years ago they were a genuine contender, a team good enough to win almost anything, forever running into the one obstacle nobody in that era could clear: [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch) and their dynasty. When that door stayed shut, Opal faded, and for three long years they were an afterthought, a name from a bygone age.

Now, out of nowhere, they are reborn. This is not a fluke run by a plucky underdog. This is a former powerhouse rediscovering its best form at exactly the right moment, and doing it in devastating fashion. The core did the damage, with [lumi.nyaa](#/player/lumi-nyaa) leading the fragging, [joyyy_cheng](#/player/joyyy-cheng) marshalling the team from the caller's chair, and [kuro_mi](#/player/kuro-mi) chipping in alongside the double-AWP look of [Seireiix](#/player/seireiix) and [Scorpium](#/player/scorpium). They did not just win. They looked like a team that belongs at the very top.

The numbers back it up. [Opal](#/team/opal) have surged up the rankings on the back of an eight-match winning streak of their own, and for the first time in three years they look every bit the contender they once were. The dark horses were tamed, the streak was broken, and the newcomers were denied. This was Opal's day, and on this evidence, it may be the first of many. The old guard is back.
